T0800.name: Activate Firmware Update Mode
T0800.summary: Adversaries may activate firmware update mode on devices to prevent expected response functions from engaging in reaction to an emergency or process malfunction.

T0801.name: Monitor Process State
T0801.summary: Adversaries may gather information about the physical process state.

T0802.name: Automated Collection
T0802.summary: Adversaries may automate collection of industrial environment information using tools or scripts.

T0806.name: Brute Force I/O
T0806.summary: Adversaries may repetitively or successively change I/O point values to perform an action.

T0807.name: Command-Line Interface
T0807.summary: Adversaries may utilize command-line interfaces (CLIs) to interact with systems and execute commands.

T0809.name: Data Destruction
T0809.summary: Adversaries may perform data destruction over the course of an operation.

T0811.name: Data from Information Repositories
T0811.summary: Adversaries may target and collect data from information repositories.

T0813.name: Denial of Control
T0813.summary: Adversaries may cause a denial of control to temporarily prevent operators and engineers from interacting with process controls.

T0814.name: Denial of Service
T0814.summary: Adversaries may perform Denial-of-Service (DoS) attacks to disrupt expected device functionality.

T0815.name: Denial of View
T0815.summary: Adversaries may cause a denial of view in attempt to disrupt and prevent operator oversight on the status of an ICS environment.

T0816.name: Device Restart/Shutdown
T0816.summary: Adversaries may forcibly restart or shutdown a device in an ICS environment to disrupt and potentially negatively impact physical processes.

T0817.name: Drive-by Compromise
T0817.summary: Adversaries may gain access to a system during a drive-by compromise, when a user visits a website as part of a regular browsing session.

T0819.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
T0819.summary: Adversaries may leverage weaknesses to exploit internet-facing software for initial access into an industrial network.

T0820.name: Exploitation for Evasion
T0820.summary: Adversaries may exploit a software vulnerability to take advantage of a programming error in a program, service, or within the operating system software or kernel itself to evade detection.

T0821.name: Modify Controller Tasking
T0821.summary: Adversaries may modify the tasking of a controller to allow for the execution of their own programs.

T0822.name: External Remote Services
T0822.summary: Adversaries may leverage external remote services as a point of initial access into your network.

T0823.name: Graphical User Interface
T0823.summary: Adversaries may attempt to gain access to a machine via a Graphical User Interface (GUI) to enhance execution capabilities.

T0826.name: Loss of Availability
T0826.summary: Adversaries may attempt to disrupt essential components or systems to prevent owner and operator from delivering products or services.

T0827.name: Loss of Control
T0827.summary: Adversaries may seek to achieve a sustained loss of control or a runaway condition in which operators cannot issue any commands even if the malicious interference has subsided.

T0828.name: Loss of Productivity and Revenue
T0828.summary: Adversaries may cause loss of productivity and revenue through disruption and even damage to the availability and integrity of control system operations, devices, and related processes.

T0829.name: Loss of View
T0829.summary: Adversaries may cause a sustained or permanent loss of view where the ICS equipment will require local, hands-on operator intervention; for instance, a restart or manual operation.

T0830.name: Adversary-in-the-Middle
T0830.summary: Adversaries with privileged network access may seek to modify network traffic in real time using adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) attacks.

T0831.name: Manipulation of Control
T0831.summary: Adversaries may manipulate physical process control within the industrial environment.

T0832.name: Manipulation of View
T0832.summary: Adversaries may attempt to manipulate the information reported back to operators or controllers.

T0834.name: Native API
T0834.summary: Adversaries may directly interact with the native OS application programming interface (API) to access system functions.

T0835.name: Manipulate I/O Image
T0835.summary: Adversaries may manipulate the I/O image of PLCs through various means to prevent them from functioning as expected.

T0836.name: Modify Parameter
T0836.summary: Adversaries may modify parameters used to instruct industrial control system devices.

T0837.name: Loss of Protection
T0837.summary: Adversaries may compromise protective system functions designed to prevent the effects of faults and abnormal conditions.

T0838.name: Modify Alarm Settings
T0838.summary: Adversaries may modify alarm settings to prevent alerts that may inform operators of their presence or to prevent responses to dangerous and unintended scenarios.

T0840.name: Network Connection Enumeration
T0840.summary: Adversaries may perform network connection enumeration to discover information about device communication patterns.

T0842.name: Network Sniffing
T0842.summary: An adversary may attempt to sniff the traffic to gain information about the target.

T0843.name: Program Download
T0843.summary: Adversaries may perform a program download to transfer a user program to a controller.

T0843.001.name: Download All
T0843.001.summary: Adversaries may execute a full program download to a PLC to overwrite the entire PLC program and configuration to deploy a new project or make major changes.

T0843.002.name: Online Edit
T0843.002.summary: Adversaries may execute an online edit of a PLC to update parts of an existing program.

T0843.003.name: Program Append
T0843.003.summary: Adversaries may execute a program append to a PLC to update parts of an existing program.

T0845.name: Program Upload
T0845.summary: Adversaries may attempt to upload a program from a PLC to gather information about an industrial process.

T0846.name: Remote System Discovery
T0846.summary: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of other systems by IP address, hostname, or other logical identifier on a network that may be used for subsequent Lateral Movement or Discovery techniques.

T0846.001.name: Port Scan
T0846.001.summary: Adversaries may perform a port scan on a system, device, or network to identify live hosts, enumerate open ports and running services, identify operating systems, and map out the network.

T0846.002.name: Broadcast Discovery
T0846.002.summary: Adversaries may perform broadcast discovery requests to enumerate systems and devices on a network.

T0846.003.name: Multicast Discovery
T0846.003.summary: Adversaries may perform multicast discovery requests which is when one system or device sends messages to all systems and devices in a pre-defined group on a network (or subnet) and then waits for a response.

T0847.name: Replication Through Removable Media
T0847.summary: Adversaries may move onto systems, such as those separated from the enterprise network, by copying malware to removable media which is inserted into the control systems environment.

T0848.name: Rogue Master
T0848.summary: Adversaries may setup a rogue master to leverage control server functions to communicate with outstations.

T0849.name: Masquerading
T0849.summary: Adversaries may use masquerading to disguise a malicious application or executable as another file, to avoid operator and engineer suspicion.

T0851.name: Rootkit
T0851.summary: Adversaries may deploy rootkits to hide the presence of programs, files, network connections, services, drivers, and other system components.

T0852.name: Screen Capture
T0852.summary: Adversaries may attempt to perform screen capture of devices in the control system environment.

T0853.name: Scripting
T0853.summary: Adversaries may use scripting languages to execute arbitrary code in the form of a pre-written script or in the form of user-supplied code to an interpreter.

T0858.name: Change Operating Mode
T0858.summary: Adversaries may change the operating mode of a controller to gain additional access to engineering functions such as Program Download.

T0859.name: Valid Accounts
T0859.summary: Adversaries may steal the credentials of a specific user or service account using credential access techniques.

T0860.name: Wireless Compromise
T0860.summary: Adversaries may perform wireless compromise as a method of gaining communications and unauthorized access to a wireless network.

T0861.name: Point & Tag Identification
T0861.summary: Adversaries may collect point and tag values to gain a more comprehensive understanding of the process environment.

T0862.name: Supply Chain Compromise
T0862.summary: Adversaries may perform supply chain compromise to gain control systems environment access by means of infected products, software, and workflows.

T0863.name: User Execution
T0863.summary: Adversaries may rely on a targeted organizations user interaction for the execution of malicious code.

T0864.name: Transient Cyber Asset
T0864.summary: Adversaries may target devices that are transient across ICS networks and external networks.

T0865.name: Spearphishing Attachment
T0865.summary: Adversaries may use a spearphishing attachment, a variant of spearphishing, as a form of a social engineering attack against specific targets.

T0866.name: Exploitation of Remote Services
T0866.summary: Adversaries may exploit a software vulnerability to take advantage of a programming error in a program, service, or within the operating system software or kernel itself to enable remote service abuse.

T0867.name: Lateral Tool Transfer
T0867.summary: Adversaries may transfer tools or other files from one system to another to stage adversary tools or other files over the course of an operation.

T0868.name: Detect Operating Mode
T0868.summary: Adversaries may gather information about a PLCs or controllers current operating mode.

T0869.name: Standard Application Layer Protocol
T0869.summary: Adversaries may establish command and control capabilities over commonly used application layer protocols such as HTTP(S), OPC, RDP, telnet, DNP3, and modbus.

T0871.name: Execution through API
T0871.summary: Adversaries may attempt to leverage Application Program Interfaces (APIs) used for communication between control software and the hardware.

T0872.name: Indicator Removal on Host
T0872.summary: Adversaries may attempt to remove indicators of their presence on a system in an effort to cover their tracks.

T0873.name: Project File Infection
T0873.summary: Adversaries may attempt to infect project files with malicious code.

T0873.001.name: Siemens Project File Format
T0873.001.summary: Adversaries may infect Siemens PLC project files (i.e., Step 7, WinCC, etc.) to achieve Execution, Persistence, and Lateral Movement objectives.

T0874.name: Hooking
T0874.summary: Adversaries may hook into application programming interface (API) functions used by processes to redirect calls for execution and privilege escalation means.

T0877.name: I/O Image
T0877.summary: Adversaries may seek to capture process values related to the inputs and outputs of a PLC. During the scan cycle, a PLC reads the status of all inputs and stores them in an image table.

T0878.name: Alarm Suppression
T0878.summary: Adversaries may target protection function alarms to prevent them from notifying operators of critical conditions.

T0879.name: Damage to Property
T0879.summary: Adversaries may cause damage and destruction of property to infrastructure, equipment, and the surrounding environment when attacking control systems.

T0880.name: Loss of Safety
T0880.summary: Adversaries may compromise safety system functions designed to maintain safe operation of a process when unacceptable or dangerous conditions occur.

T0881.name: Service Stop
T0881.summary: Adversaries may stop or disable services on a system to render those services unavailable to legitimate users.

T0882.name: Theft of Operational Information
T0882.summary: Adversaries may steal operational information on a production environment as a direct mission outcome for personal gain or to inform future operations.

T0883.name: Internet Accessible Device
T0883.summary: Adversaries may gain access into industrial environments through systems exposed directly to the internet for remote access rather than through External Remote Services.

T0884.name: Connection Proxy
T0884.summary: Adversaries may use a connection proxy to direct network traffic between systems or act as an intermediary for network communications.

T0885.name: Commonly Used Port
T0885.summary: Adversaries may communicate over a commonly used port to bypass firewalls or network detection systems and to blend in with normal network activity, to avoid more detailed inspection.

T0886.name: Remote Services
T0886.summary: Adversaries may leverage remote services to move between assets and network segments.

T0887.name: Wireless Sniffing
T0887.summary: Adversaries may seek to capture radio frequency (RF) communication used for remote control and reporting in distributed environments.

T0888.name: Remote System Information Discovery
T0888.summary: An adversary may attempt to get detailed information about remote systems and their peripherals, such as make/model, role, and configuration.

T0889.name: Modify Program
T0889.summary: Adversaries may modify or add a program on a controller to affect how it interacts with the physical process, peripheral devices and other hosts on the network.

T0890.name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
T0890.summary: Adversaries may exploit software vulnerabilities in an attempt to elevate privileges.

T0892.name: Change Credential
T0892.summary: Adversaries may modify software and device credentials to prevent operator and responder access.

T0893.name: Data from Local System
T0893.summary: Adversaries may target and collect data from local system sources, such as file systems, configuration files, or local databases.

T0894.name: System Binary Proxy Execution
T0894.summary: Adversaries may bypass process and/or signature-based defenses by proxying execution of malicious content with signed, or otherwise trusted, binaries.

T0895.name: Autorun Image
T0895.summary: Adversaries may leverage AutoRun functionality or scripts to execute malicious code.

T1691.name: Block Operational Technology Message
T1691.summary: Adversaries may block messages between systems and devices in an OT/ICS environment to disrupt processes.

T1691.001.name: Command Message
T1691.001.summary: Adversaries may block a command message from reaching its intended target to prevent command execution.

T1691.002.name: Reporting Message
T1691.002.summary: Adversaries may block or prevent a reporting message from reaching its intended target.

T1692.name: Unauthorized Message
T1692.summary: Adversaries may send unauthorized messages to ICS systems and devices to evade defenses or manipulate processes.

T1692.001.name: Command Message
T1692.001.summary: Adversaries may send unauthorized command messages to instruct control system assets to perform actions outside of their intended functionality, or without the logical preconditions to trigger their expected function.

T1692.002.name: Reporting Message
T1692.002.summary: Adversaries may spoof reporting messages in control system environments for evasion and to impair process control.

T1693.name: Modify Firmware
T1693.summary: Adversaries may modify firmware on a system or device by installing malicious or vulnerable versions that enable them to achieve objectives such as Persistence, Impair Process Control, and Inhibit Response Function.

T1693.001.name: System Firmware
T1693.001.summary: An adversary may exploit the firmware update feature on accessible devices to upload malicious or out-of-date firmware.

T1693.002.name: Module Firmware
T1693.002.summary: Adversaries may install malicious or vulnerable firmware onto modular hardware devices.

T1694.name: Insecure Credentials
T1694.summary: Adversaries may target insecure credentials as a means to persist on a system or device or move laterally from one system or device to another.

T1694.001.name: Default Credentials
T1694.001.summary: Adversaries may leverage manufacturer or supplier set default credentials on control system devices.

T1694.002.name: Hardcoded Credentials
T1694.002.summary: Adversaries may leverage credentials that are hardcoded in software or firmware to gain an unauthorized interactive user session to an asset.

T1695.name: Block Communications
T1695.summary: Adversaries may block communications to prevent reporting messages and command messages from reaching their intended target devices disrupting processes, operations, and causing cyber-physical impacts.

T1695.001.name: Serial COM
T1695.001.summary: Adversaries may block access to serial COM to prevent instructions or configurations from reaching target devices.

T1695.002.name: Ethernet
T1695.002.summary: Adversaries may block access to Ethernet communications to prevent instructions or configurations messages from reaching target systems and devices.

T1695.003.name: Wi-Fi
T1695.003.summary: Adversaries may block access to Wi-Fi communications to prevent messages from reaching target systems and devices.

mitigations.M0942: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
